Nourishment
NUR-ish-ment
n. (that which feeds and sustains; supply ministered to a body)
Greek epichoregeo, to supply or minister, underlies the phrase; the noun in the Authorized Version renders the idea of nutriment conveyed through joints and bands. The English comes through Old French norrir, from Latin nutrire, to feed.

Biblical Definition

And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God. The picture is a body fed from its head, and every term in it is load-bearing. Nourishment is not generated by the members; it is ministered to them, supplied from outside and above, and it reaches them through joints and bands — that is, through the ordinary connective structure of the body, not by private channels. Growth follows: the body increaseth with the increase of God, a growth that is God's own giving and not the members' achievement. Paul states it negatively because he is describing men who had let go: not holding the Head. A member may keep the appearance of life for a while after the supply is cut, but it will not grow, and it will not live. The Lord says the same thing in his own figure — I am the vine, ye are the branches; for without me ye can do nothing. Two practical conclusions follow for the Christian and for the congregation. Nourishment comes from Christ, so no substitute will feed. And it comes through the joints and bands, so the member that detaches itself from the body has cut the very channel by which Christ feeds him.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): that which serves to promote the growth of animals or plants, or to repair the waste of animal bodies; nutriment; food; sustenance.

expand to see more

NOURISHMENT, n. That which serves to promote the growth of animals or plants, or to repair the waste of animal bodies; food; sustenance; nutriment.

NOURISHMENT, n. Nutrition; support of animal or vegetable life and growth.

NOURISH, v.t. To feed and cause to grow; to supply a living being with matter which increases its bulk or supplies the waste occasioned by any of the animal functions.

MINISTER, v.t. To give; to afford; to supply.

KNIT, v.t. To unite closely; to connect; to join.

Key Scripture

Colossians 2:19 — "And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God."

Ephesians 4:15 — "But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:"

John 15:5 — "I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing."

1 Peter 2:2 — "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:"

Modern Corruption

Spiritual nourishment is widely relocated from Christ ministered through word, ordinances, and the body, to whatever a believer finds personally sustaining; and the joints and bands are treated as optional.

expand to see more

The individualized account of Christian growth treats the church as a resource a believer may use if he finds it helpful. Colossians 2:19 makes the body the channel, not the accessory. Nourishment is ministered by joints and bands — through the preached word, the ordinances, the oversight of elders, the mutual service of members. A man who has severed those connections has not chosen a leaner diet; he has cut the supply line. The regulative principle is not fussiness about forms but the recognition that God has appointed the means by which he feeds his people, and that no substitute of our devising carries the nutriment.

A second substitution is subtler and comes from within the churches: nourishment identified with experience — the felt encounter, the moving service, the sense of having been fed — rather than with Christ held by faith through his appointed means. Peter says the milk is of the word, and Paul locates the supply in the Head. Where a congregation begins to measure its feeding by intensity rather than by Christ delivered in the Scriptures, it will keep the sensation for a season and lose the growth, because the increase in view is the increase of God and God has said where he gives it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek epichoregeo (G2023), to supply abundantly; haphe (G860), a joint or band of union; sumbibazo (G4822), to knit together; auxano (G837), to grow or increase.

expand to see more

Greek epichoregeo (G2023) — to supply, to minister to; the supply comes from the Head, not from the member.

Greek haphe (G860) — a fastening, a joint; the ordinary connective structure through which supply passes.

Greek sumbibazo (G4822) — to knit or join together; rendered knit together.

Greek auxano (G837) — to grow, to increase; the growth is God's own increase.

Greek kephale (G2776) — head; Christ as the Head of the body, the church.

Usage

"“having nourishment ministered” — supplied, not self-generated."

"“by joints and bands” — through the ordinary connective life of the body."

"“increaseth with the increase of God” — growth that God gives."
